//: Typecheck config for the AGS config's PURE-MODULE unit tests.
WHY IT EXISTS. `dotfiles/config/ags/` shipped with no TypeScript test
setup at all: `make capture-test` covers the capture TOOL's domain and
nothing covers the ags config's own pure modules. The battery panel's
presentation decisions (time wording, duration formatting, profile icon
selection, active-row matching) are exactly the kind of logic that reads
fine and is wrong in an edge case, and they are pure TypeScript -- so they
are testable without the desktop stack, which is the whole point of
keeping them out of the widget.
SEPARATE FROM ANY APP CONFIG, ON PURPOSE. This file typechecks the TESTS.
It needs @types/node for `node:test`/`node:assert`, and
`allowImportingTsExtensions` because the test files import the modules
under test with an explicit `.ts` suffix (see the resolve-hook note below).
It deliberately does NOT widen to `gi://*` or `ags/*`: nothing reachable
from here may import GTK, which is what keeps the suite runnable on a
stock CI runner with no AGS and no GTK4 installed.
WHERE @types/node COMES FROM. `make ags-test` installs it into THIS
directory's own node_modules on demand (its ags-test-deps target), exactly
as `make capture-test` installs @types/node under
src/gui-tools/capture-tool/tests/. The install MUST be a SIBLING of this
config rather than a child: tsc's default typeRoots walk starts at the
config's own directory and walks UP, so tests/node_modules/@types is found
and tests/ts/node_modules/@types is not (it resolves to TS2688).
`"types": ["node"]` is a DECLARED
dependency, not a request for whatever the machine happens to have:
without the install this config cannot compile at all (TS2688).
tests/node_modules/ is gitignored -- a committed node_modules is both a
deployment hazard and, here, a machine artefact.
WHY THE EXPLICIT `.ts` SUFFIX. Node runs these files natively via its
built-in TypeScript type-stripping (node >= 22.6, unflagged from 22.18 for
`.ts`). Node's ESM resolver does NOT do extensionless lookup, so
`import ... from "../../components/battery/presentation"` would fail at
RUNTIME. The suffix is load-bearing, not a style choice, and
allowImportingTsExtensions is what lets tsc agree with Node.
resolve-hooks.mjs additionally teaches Node the ONE thing the `ags bundle`
bundler already does -- append `.ts` to a relative specifier that misses --
so app-side sources may keep idiomatic extensionless imports and the
workaround stays in test-only infrastructure.
`noEmit` is set and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` is deliberately NOT
used: nothing here is ever emitted. These files are executed by Node, not
bundled by ags.
THE MODULE LIST IS EXPLICIT, NOT A GLOB, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
`components/**/*.ts` would drag in `components/wifi/state.ts` (imports
`ags`) and `services/**/*.ts` would drag in `wifi-service.ts`,
`nm-client.ts`, `speedtest-service.ts`, `bluetooth-service.ts` and
`mpris-service.ts` (all import `gi://*`) -- every one of which fails to
compile here and, worse, would quietly turn this suite into a suite that
cannot run without the desktop stack. `mpris-core.ts` is listed because it
is the one genuinely pure module under services/ today. A new pure module
is added here BY NAME, which is the moment its author states in the repo
that it is pure -- the list IS the purity contract.
THE PLATFORM IS NOW AN EXTERNAL BARE SPECIFIER (spine AD-17). The ports
(`event-client`, `icon-source`, `notifier`, `preferences`, `reactive`,
`theme`) and their pure tests MOVED to the `ags-platform` repo, which owns
and gates them (`make test` / `typecheck-tests` there). This config no longer
lists `../platform/ports/*` and no longer ships the duplicate port suites --
the platform's own suite IS the coverage, and duplicating it here would test
external code from the app repo (AD-1: apps -> platform only).
WHAT STAYS, AND WHY IT CAN STILL RUN. The bar-specific pure modules stay: the
battery/audio/network presentation logic, the layout vocabulary, `kit/shapes`
and the four `domains/*/read-model.ts` cores. A bar module that needs a
platform TYPE imports it by bare specifier (`ags-platform/ports/reactive`);
those are `import type`, so Node's type-stripping ERASES them at runtime and
the suite still runs with no platform code loaded. `icon-state-keys.test.ts`
and `kit-shapes.test.ts` do import platform VALUES (`iconByStateKey`, ...);
they resolve through the dev `node_modules/ags-platform` shortcut that
`make ags-platform-dev` creates, whose target sits OUTSIDE node_modules so
Node's type-stripping accepts the `.ts` sources (it realpaths the symlink).
This is the decided test-import mechanism: NO resolve hook, because a symlink
to a checkout outside node_modules is enough and keeps the app's sources
idiomatic.
`kit/shapes.ts` deliberately leaves the rendered subtree type opaque (a type
parameter, default `unknown`) instead of naming `JSX.Element`, so it carries
no JSX runtime; `kit/widget.tsx` specializes it to gnim's `JSX.Element` for
the app.
The four `domains/*/read-model.ts` cores are the network/battery/bluetooth/
audio read models. They are pure BY CONSTRUCTION: each takes its Astal
service and its reactive runtime as parameters, so the Astal bindings live
in the sibling `domains/*/astal.ts` adapters, which are deliberately NOT
listed here (they import gi://* and ags and belong to the app program).
